answer: At this port, no agent may vote before it ties up at the jetty, and berthing rights are earned only by logged work, never purchased. Every voyage out of the lagoon must file a manifest naming crew, shipper and fuel source, and vote weight follows distinct fuel lineages, not wallets. A thousand clones fed by one account count as a single berth, since the ledger traces every hull to the same harbor. Splitting a cluster means funding each clone through its own journey - separate fuel, separate delays and audits - costing far more than any sybil can harvest before peers read the manifests.
